items: Schedule professional HVAC tune-ups in spring and fall to catch system failures before they happen and extend equipment lifespan.
Inspect your roof in spring using binoculars or by walking the perimeter to spot missing shingles or sagging areas before rainy season arrives.
Clean dryer vent lines annually by pulling out the dryer, disconnecting the vent, and removing all lint buildup to prevent house fires.
Inspect exterior trim and siding in summer when dry weather allows you to paint or patch any rot, peeling paint, or pest entry points.
Schedule a furnace inspection before heating season to check the heat exchanger for carbon monoxide risks and verify safety controls are functioning.
Book a sewer scope if your home is over 20 years old to catch tree roots and pipe degradation before they cause a backup costing thousands.
Test smoke and CO detectors by pressing the test button on every unit, replacing batteries and any detectors over 10 years old—this takes 10 minutes and saves lives.
Disaster-proof your home by disconnecting outdoor hoses, closing faucet shut-offs, and blowing out irrigation lines before freezing temperatures arrive.
Clean gutters twice yearly in spring and fall to prevent roof leaks, foundation damage, and basement flooding in that order.
Apply fresh caulk and weatherstripping around windows, doors, and utility penetrations each fall to eliminate drafts and maximize energy efficiency.
Lubricate garage door springs, cables, and rollers with silicone spray to prevent failure and ensure smooth operation year-round.
Run each irrigation zone in summer to identify broken heads, underground leaks, and overspray onto the house before you get a shocking water bill.
